verdict.rationale: Granola ships a documented REST API with a published OpenAPI 3.1 spec. It covers notes, transcripts, folders, spaces, audit, webhook endpoints and legal holds, and access is scoped by note-access key scopes. However, nothing shows UI parity: Chat, recipes, templates, recording/transcription, follow-up email drafting, sharing and deletion are documented only as UI features. API keys are also limited to Business/Enterprise plans. Missing for 10: evidence that UI actions (chat, recipes, templates, note creation/recording, sharing, deletion, settings) are exposed via the API, an explicit parity commitment, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: /v1 endpoints for notes, transcripts, folders, spaces, audit, webhook-endpoints, and legal holds
The Granola API lets you build custom integrations with programmatic access to meeting notes, transcripts, and AI summaries.
When you create an API key, you choose which note access scopes it should include.
